Bi-variate choropleth map comparing the estimated percent of the population 65 and older and 17 and younger in the Contiguous United States by county, 2020

The [dependency ratio](/wiki/Dependency_ratio "Dependency ratio") is the age-population ratio of people who are normally not in the labor force (the dependent population, which includes those aged 0 to 14 and 65 and older) to those who are (the productive part, ages 15 to 64). It is used to gauge the strain on the populace that is productive. The support ratio is the ratio of the working-age population to the elderly population, that is, the reciprocal of the aged dependency ratio.

[Howard Shore](/wiki/Howard_Shore "Howard Shore") composed, orchestrated, conducted and produced the trilogy's music. Shore visited the set in 1999, and composed a version of the Shire theme and Frodo's Theme before Jackson began shooting.[[50]](#cite_note-50) In August 2000, he visited the set again and watched the assembly cuts of *The Fellowship of the Ring* and *The Return of the King*.[[51]](#cite_note-51) In the music, Shore included many (85 to 110) [leitmotifs](/wiki/Leitmotifs "Leitmotifs") to represent various characters, cultures and places—the largest catalogue of leitmotifs in the history of cinema, surpassing, for comparison, that of the entire [*Star Wars* film series](/wiki/Music_of_Star_Wars "Music of Star Wars"). For example, there are multiple leitmotifs just for the hobbits and the [Shire](/wiki/Shire_(Middle-earth) "Shire (Middle-earth)"). Breast cancer screening can be instrumental, given that the size of a breast cancer and its spread are among the most critical factors in predicting the prognosis of the disease. Breast cancers found during screening are typically smaller and less likely to have spread outside the breast.[[10]](#cite_note-10) Training health workers to do clinical breast examination may have potential to detect breast cancer at an early stage.[[11]](#cite_note-11) A 2013 [Cochrane review](/wiki/Cochrane_review "Cochrane review") found that it was unclear whether [mammographic](/wiki/Mammograph "Mammograph") screening does more harm than good, in that a large proportion of women who test positive turn out not to have the disease.[[12]](#cite_note-Got2013-12) A 2009 review for the [US Preventive Services Task Force](/wiki/US_Preventive_Services_Task_Force "US Preventive Services Task Force") found evidence of benefit in those 40 to 70 years of age,[[13]](#cite_note-13) and the organization recommends screening every two years in women ages 50 to 74.[[14]](#cite_note-USPSTFScreen2016-14)

The medications [tamoxifen](/wiki/Tamoxifen "Tamoxifen") or [raloxifene](/wiki/Raloxifene "Raloxifene") may be used in an effort to prevent breast cancer in those who are at high risk of developing it.[[2]](#cite_note-WCR2014-2) [Surgical removal of both breasts](/wiki/Preventive_mastectomy "Preventive mastectomy") is another preventive measure in some high risk women.[[2]](#cite_note-WCR2014-2) In those who have been diagnosed with cancer, several treatments may be used, including surgery, [radiation therapy](/wiki/Radiation_therapy "Radiation therapy"), [chemotherapy](/wiki/Chemotherapy "Chemotherapy"), [hormonal therapy](/wiki/Hormonal_therapy_(oncology) "Hormonal therapy (oncology)"), and [targeted therapy](/wiki/Targeted_therapy "Targeted therapy").[[1]](#cite_note-NCI2014Pt-1) Types of surgery vary from [breast-conserving surgery](/wiki/Breast-conserving_su

Pyne Hall, where the first female students lived on campus

Princeton explicitly prohibited the admission of women from its founding in 1746 until 1969. Since it lacked an affiliated women's college, it was often referred to as a "monastery", both lovingly and derisively, by members of the Princeton community.[[150]](#cite_note-Markham-1962-152)[[151]](#cite_note-153)
For about a decade, from 1887 to 1897, nearby [Evelyn College for Women](/wiki/Evelyn_College_for_Women "Evelyn College for Women") was largely composed of daughters of professors and sisters of Princeton undergraduates. While no legal connection existed, many Princeton professors taught there and several Princeton administrators, such as Francis Patton, were on its board of trustees. It closed in 1897 following the death of its founder, [Joshua McIlvaine](/wiki/Joshua_Hall_McIlvaine "Joshua Hall McIlvaine").[[152]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELeitch1978170–171-154)

In 1947, three female members of the library staff enrolled in beginning Russian courses to deal with an increase in Russian literature in the library.[[113]](#cite_note-Princeton-Library-114) In 1961, Princeton admitted its first female graduate student, Sabra Follett Meservey,[[150]](#cite_note-Markham-1962-152) who would go on to be the first woman to earn a master's degree at Princeton.[[113]](#cite_note-Princeton-Library-114) Meservey was, at the time of her admission, already a member of the faculty at Douglass College within Princeton. The **Empire State Building** is a 102-story,[[c]](#cite_note-Floor_count-10) [supertall](/wiki/Supertall "Supertall") skyscraper in the [Midtown South](/wiki/Midtown_South "Midtown South") neighborhood of [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"), New York City, United States. The building was designed in the [Art Deco](/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") style by [Shreve, Lamb & Harmon](/wiki/Shreve,_Lamb_%26_Harmon "Shreve, Lamb & Harmon") and constructed between 1930 and 1931. Its name is derived from "[Empire State](/wiki/Empire_State "Empire State")", the [nickname](/wiki/List_of_U.S._state_nicknames "List of U.S. state nicknames") of New York state. The building has a roof height of 1,250 feet (380 m) and stands a total of 1,454 feet (443.2 m) tall including its [antenna](/wiki/Antenna_(radio) "Antenna (radio)"). The Empire State Building was the world's tallest building until the [North Tower](/wiki/1_World_Trade_Center_(1970%E2%80%932001) "1 World Trade Center (1970–2001)") of the [World Trade Center](/wiki/World_Trade_Center_(1973%E2%80%932001) "World Trade Center (1973–2001)") was [topped out in 1970](/wiki/Construction_of_the_World_Trade_Center "Construction of the World Trade Center"); following the [September 11 attacks](/wiki/Collapse_of_the_World_Trade_Center "Collapse of the World Trade Center") in 2001, the Empire State Building was once more New York City's tallest building until it was surpassed in 2012 by [One World Trade Center](/wiki/One_World_Trade_Center "One World Trade Center"). As of 2025, the building is the [eighth-tallest building in New York City](/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_New_York_City "List of tallest buildings in New York City"), the [tenth-tallest completed skyscraper in the United States](/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_the_United_States "List of tallest buildings in the United States"), and the [59th-tallest completed skyscraper in the world](/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings "List

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8b/Spurs_vs_Arsenal%2C_Avril_2007.jpg/330px-Spurs_vs_Arsenal%2C_Avril_2007.jpg)](/wiki/File:Spurs_vs_Arsenal,_Avril_2007.jpg)

Just before a [North London derby](/wiki/North_London_derby "North London derby") between Spurs and Arsenal in 2007.

Initially, football in London was dominated by amateur teams, drawing their membership from former [public schoolboys](/wiki/Public_school_(UK) "Public school (UK)") but gradually working-class sides came to the forefront. Royal Arsenal was London's first professional team, becoming so in 1891,[[9]](#cite_note-10) a move which saw them boycotted by the amateur London Football Association. Other London clubs soon followed Arsenal's footsteps in turning professional, including [Millwall](/wiki/Millwall_F.C. "Millwall F.C.") (1893), [Tottenham Hotspur](/wiki/Tottenham_Hotspur "Tottenham Hotspur") (1895), Fulham (1898) and [West Ham](/wiki/West_Ham_United "West Ham United") (1898).

In the meantime, Woolwich Arsenal (formerly Royal Arsenal) went on to be the first London club to join the Football League, in 1893. The following year, the [Southern League](/wiki/Southern_Football_League "Southern Football League") was founded and many of its members would go on to join the Football League. In 1901 Tottenham Hotspur became the first club from London to win the FA Cup in the professional era, although it would not be until 1931 that a London side would win the Football League, the team in question being Arsenal (having moved to [Highbury](/wiki/Arsenal_Stadium "Arsenal Stadium") in 1913 and dropping the "Woolwich" from their name).

Main article: [Padres-Dodgers rivalry](/wiki/Padres-Dodgers_rivalry "Padres-Dodgers rivalry")

The [Padres](/wiki/San_Diego_Padres "San Diego Padres")' rivalry with the Dodgers has often been lopsided in favor of Los Angeles; however, recent growth between the two teams in competition has added intensity on top of proximity between Los Angeles and San Diego.[[69]](#cite_note-70)[[70]](#cite_note-71)

The Dodgers currently lead the series 518–419, with the two teams meeting in the playoffs three times.[[71]](#cite_note-72) The Dodgers swept the Padres in the [2020 NLDS](/wiki/2020_NLDS "2020 NLDS"), won in five games in the [2024 NLDS](/wiki/2024_NLDS "2024 NLDS"), and the Padres won in four games in the [2022 NLDS](/wiki/2022_NLDS "2022 NLDS").[[72]](#cite_note-73)
